entities.summary: The Singapore Army is the land service branch of the Singapore Armed Forces (SAF). The largest of the four branches of the SAF, the Singapore Army traces its origins to the 1st Battalion, Singapore Infantry Regiment, which was formed in 1957, under British colonial rule. After Singapore's independence on 9 August 1965, the Singapore Army Bill was passed in Parliament on 23 December 1965, and National Service (NS) was subsequently introduced in 1967. Mostly made up of conscripts, the Singapore Army can mobilise all operationally-ready military reservists in the event of war or national exigencies.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Singapore Army's introduction of National Service in 1967 led to a highly disciplined and operationally-ready military force, which has been instrumental in maintaining regional stability and security. Its legacy continues to shape the country's defense strategy and national identity.
